note: The printer can take a preformatted assembly string from the instruction object, so input-controlled decode state reaches the output path here.
The safety obligation is that the copied assembly text must be fully initialized and valid before being copied into the output buffer; otherwise later printing can consume uninitialized bytes.
When no preformatted string is present, the printer formats operands through the instruction printer, which is where the uninitialized operand state is observed by the sanitizer.
